response.sql: WITH patient_avgs AS (SELECT l.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.ALB - l.TP) as patient_ALB_minus_TP, AVG(l.APPT - l.PT) as patient_APPT_minus_PT FROM Laboratory l INNER JOIN Patient p ON l.ID = p.ID GROUP BY l.ID, p.SEX), sex_avgs AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(patient_ALB_minus_TP) as sex_avg_ALB_minus_TP, AVG(patient_APPT_minus_PT) as sex_avg_APPT_minus_PT FROM patient_avgs GROUP BY SEX), overall_mean AS (SELECT AVG(sex_avg_APPT_minus_PT) as mean FROM sex_avgs), filtered_sexes AS (SELECT sex_avg_ALB_minus_TP, sex_avg_APPT_minus_PT FROM sex_avgs s CROSS JOIN overall_mean o WHERE s.sex_avg_APPT_minus_PT > o.mean) SELECT AVG(sex_avg_ALB_minus_TP) as avg_ALB_minus_TP, AVG(sex_avg_APPT_minus_PT) as avg_APPT_minus_PT, AVG(sex_avg_APPT_minus_PT) - (SELECT mean FROM overall_mean) as exceeds_mean FROM filtered_sexes

assumptions.assumption: The Laboratory table column is APPT—text formatting makes it ambiguous whether this is spelled with double-P or double-T, but the medical context (Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time) suggests APPT.
'Above the mean' is interpreted as strictly greater than (>) rather than ≥.
